Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

Liberal Democrat Manifesto 2010 – Summary (under 500 words)

Core aim: “Hard‑wire fairness” into national life by redistributing power and opportunity. Four priorities:
- Fair taxes that put money back in your pocket
- A fair chance for every child
- A fair future by creating green jobs and rebuilding the economy
- A fair deal by cleaning up politics and restoring civil liberties

Tax and public finances
- Raise the income tax personal allowance to £10,000 (c. £700 cut for most; 3.6m taken out of tax), funded by: basic-rate tax relief on pensions only; equalising capital gains with income tax; anti‑avoidance; per‑plane duty to replace Air Passenger Duty; 1% mansion tax above £2m; reform non-dom status.
- Credible deficit plan: over £15bn identified annual savings; start cuts from 2011–12 based on economic tests; £400 cap on public-sector pay rises for two years; restrict tax credits; scrap ID cards/biometric passports; cancel Eurofighter Tranche 3B; prison reform; reduce bureaucracy; review Trident and public sector pensions; better IT procurement; establish a cross‑party Council on Financial Stability.

Economy and jobs
- Break up banks (separate retail/investment), introduce a Banking Levy, reform bonuses, get lending going, grow local/regional finance (Local Enterprise Funds, Regional Stock Exchanges).
- One‑year green stimulus to create 100,000 jobs: shipyard upgrades for offshore wind, £400 “eco cash‑back” for home upgrades, public‑building insulation, bring 250,000 empty homes into use, bus scrappage; large youth opportunity programme; 15,000 extra Foundation Degrees; support apprenticeships.
- Create a UK Infrastructure Bank to mobilise private capital for energy and transport; invest in superfast broadband; reform business rates to site-value, devolve to councils; focus RDAs on economic development or replace with local authority leadership.
- Back mutuals/co‑ops; convert Northern Rock to a building society; secure Royal Mail investment with majority public/employee ownership and Post Office in public hands.

Education and skills
- £2.5bn Pupil Premium for disadvantaged pupils to cut class sizes and fund one‑to‑one tuition; SEN assessments for all 5‑year‑olds; stronger teacher training; anti‑bullying.
- Slim down curriculum and testing; independent standards authority; combine academic/vocational routes via a General Diploma; allow 14–19 study at college; close FE/school sixth-form funding gap.
- Phase out university tuition fees over six years (final-year fees scrapped immediately); national bursary scheme; merge skills/HE funding quangos.

Health and care
- Protect frontline NHS by cutting waste: halve the Department of Health; scrap SHAs; cap top pay; integrate health and social care; expand talking therapies; prioritise dementia research; tackle alcohol harm; improve air quality.
- Patient entitlements replace central targets; staff control ward budgets; elected Local Health Boards; GP choice and email access; language/competence tests for doctors.

Families, consumers and pensions
- Shareable parental leave; fathers’ antenatal time off; extend flexible working to all; strengthen child protection and youth services.
- Restore earnings link for state pension (triple-lock style), end forced annuitisation at 75, scrap compulsory retirement ages; respite for carers; long-term care commission.
- Fairer energy tariffs with cheapest rates for essential use; social tariffs; PostBank; cap unfair bank and card charges; cut rail fares (RPI–1%), refunds for rail replacement; regulate wheel‑clamping.

Climate, environment and transport
- Zero‑carbon Britain by 2050; 40% of electricity non‑carbon by 2020 (majority offshore/marine); efficiency drive; block unabated coal; oppose new nuclear; European Supergrid; strengthen EU ETS and push EU 30% 2020 target; protect forests; zero‑waste strategy; expand access to countryside; double woodland by 2050.
- Invest in rail reopenings and capacity; empower councils to regulate buses; promote cycling/walking; replace APD with per‑plane duty; cancel Heathrow third runway; zero‑emission cars target by 2040; prepare revenue‑neutral road pricing; rural fuel discount.

Crime, justice, immigration
- 3,000 more police funded by axing ID cards; elected police authorities; cut red tape; evidence‑led drugs policy; focus on organised crime.
- Presumption against short sentences; restorative justice; prisoners work and pay victims; move addicts/mentally ill to appropriate settings; cancel mega‑prison programme.
- Firm but fair immigration: reinstate exit checks; National Border Force; regional points‑based system; crack down on rogue employers; prioritise deporting criminals; earned regularisation for long‑resident law‑abiding migrants (pre‑2010); humane asylum with independent agency; end child detention; allow asylum seekers to work.

Politics and civil liberties
- STV for Commons (reduce MPs by ~150); votes at 16; fixed terms; stronger Commons scrutiny; fully elected second chamber; written constitution via citizens’ convention; cap donations at £10k; right to recall MPs; lobbyist register; extend FOI.
- Freedom Bill: regulate CCTV; curb council surveillance; protect jury trial and protest; reform libel; scrap ID cards/biometric passports/ContactPoint; limit DNA retention to convicts; end blanket retention of internet/email data; scrap control orders; 14‑day pre‑charge limit; allow intercept evidence.

International
- Meet 0.7% aid by 2013 in law; new finance (e.g., financial transaction tax); crack down on tax havens/corruption; support debt cancellation.
- Strategic defence review; no like‑for‑like Trident replacement; strengthen European defence cooperation; improve forces’ pay and housing.
- Pro‑EU reform agenda; future in/out referendum on fundamental change; euro only by referendum when conditions allow.
- Ethical foreign policy: inquiry into torture/rendition; arms trade controls; diplomacy on Iran; support two‑state solution and end Gaza blockade; Afghanistan strategy tied to governance and regional diplomacy to bring troops home during the Parliament.

TEXT_E:
Conservative Party Manifesto 2010 – Summary (≤500 words)

Vision and values
- “Big Society, not big government”: devolve power from the centre to people, professionals and communities; rebuild trust through transparency and accountability.
- Core beliefs: responsibility (fiscal, personal, social), enterprise and aspiration, localism, fairness, and the idea that “we’re all in this together.”

Economy and public finances
- Urgent deficit reduction: emergency Budget; Office for Budget Responsibility; eliminate most structural current deficit over a Parliament.
- Immediate £6bn savings; freeze most public sector pay for a year (protecting the lowest paid); review pension age; cap high public pensions; cut ministers’ pay; reduce MPs by 10%.
- Stop Labour’s planned National Insurance “jobs tax” for most workers/employers; protect NHS and aid budgets.
- New economic model: shift from debt to saving, investment, exports, green/hi‑tech growth; improve UKTI; boost STEM and R&D (Dyson review); refocus R&D tax credits.
- Encourage saving: restore earnings link for state pension; revive occupational pensions; end near‑mandatory annuities at 75; raise IHT threshold to £1m (funded by non‑dom levy).
- Consumer finance: new Consumer Protection Agency; free national financial advice; rein in unfair credit practices.

Jobs, welfare, skills and enterprise
- Single Work Programme for all unemployed; reassess Incapacity Benefit; tougher conditionality (“work for the dole” for long‑term claimants).
- Support SMEs: NI holiday for new start‑ups’ first 10 hires; 25% of procurement to SMEs; automatic small business rate relief.
- Tax/regulation: cut corporation tax to 25% (small companies to 20%); Office of Tax Simplification; regulatory budgets.
- Skills: 400,000 new training/apprenticeship/placement places; £2,000 SME apprentice bonus; free colleges from central control; 10,000 extra university places; consider Browne review.

Infrastructure and regional growth
- High Speed Rail (phased national network); oppose Heathrow 3rd runway; reform rail franchises; promote electric vehicles; Fair Fuel Stabiliser (consult).
- Superfast broadband via infrastructure sharing; possible licence fee top‑slice; replace RDAs with local enterprise partnerships; local business rate incentives.

Banking and financial stability
- Bank levy; restore BoE prudential supervision; curb risky trading/bonuses; increase competition; “people’s bank bonus”; improve SME credit.

Green economy
- Green Investment Bank; green ISAs; carbon price floor (reformed Climate Change Levy); shift tax mix toward environmental taxes.

Big Society and families
- Big Society Bank (unclaimed assets); train community organisers; neighbourhood powers over services/planning; National Citizen Service.
- Family policy: end couple penalty; recognise marriage/civil partnerships in tax; two‑year council tax freeze; extend flexible working and shared parental leave; protect childhood from commercialisation; refocus Sure Start on neediest; 4,200 more health visitors.

NHS and social care
- Real-terms NHS funding growth; patient choice of any qualified provider; outcome transparency; GP‑led commissioning; cut admin costs by a third; scrap non‑clinical targets.
- 24/7 urgent care, stop forced A&E/maternity closures; Cancer Drugs Fund; dentistry reform; personal health/social care budgets; voluntary social‑care insurance; stronger public health with “health premium.”

Schools
- Raise teaching quality and discipline; expand Teach First/Troops to Teachers; phonics and age‑6 reading check.
- More rigorous curriculum/exams; technical academies; reform league tables/data.
- Expand academies/free schools; pupil premium; protect special schools; tougher Ofsted on weak schools.

Crime, policing and borders
- Tougher knife crime sentencing; overhaul alcohol licensing; instant anti‑social behaviour sanctions.
- Cut police paperwork; restore discretion; elected police commissioners; monthly local crime data; Border Police Force.
- Honesty in sentencing; payment‑by‑results rehabilitation; abstinence‑based drug treatment.

Politics, localism and civil liberties
- Clean up Westminster: recall MPs; rein in lobbying; cap donations via cross‑party deal; cut cost of politics; equalise constituencies; petitions to trigger debates/bills.
- Radical transparency: publish spending, salaries, contracts; curtail quangos; right to government data.
- Local power: referendums, veto high council tax; community right to buy/run services; elected city mayors; planning/local housing reforms.
- Civil liberties: scrap ID cards/National Identity Register; UK Bill of Rights; scale back vetting; limit DNA retention.

Environment and farming
- 80% emissions cut by 2050; smart grid/meters; new nuclear (no subsidy), CCS, offshore grid, marine energy; Green Deal for home efficiency.
- Protect biodiversity, fisheries reform, animal welfare; tree planting; combat illegal logging.
- Sustainable farming, CAP reform, supermarket ombudsman; badger control for bTB; waste “Responsibility Deal,” reward recycling; water and flood resilience.

Foreign policy, defence and aid
- National Security Council; SDSR; success in Afghanistan; renew Trident; fix procurement; restore Military Covenant (allowances, care, schooling, mental health).
- Liberal Conservative foreign policy: human rights; alliances (US, India, NATO, Commonwealth); prevent Iranian nukes; two‑state solution.
- Europe: no further power transfers without referendum (“referendum lock”); Sovereignty Bill; seek repatriation of some powers; never join Euro.
- Aid: legislate 0.7% of GNI by 2013; full transparency; focus on basics and poorest; £500m/yr to fight malaria; trade‑led development; Stabilisation & Reconstruction Force.
